01What this object holds

This explorer contains 462 object and container pages and 1,213 leaf sections. It covers all 44 root keys and 255 stored atom entries observed in the snapshot, after merging dynamic records into placeholder shapes.

Coverage was checked by counting every JSON value before and after normalization: 6,036 objects + 1,615 arrays + 17,725 primitive values = 25,376 occurrences. Those are source occurrences, not unique field names. The 462 pages are normalized structural shapes, not 462 user projects or sessions.

Type
object
Full path
/
Presence
One root object; 44 direct keys.
Meaning

The desktop’s persisted global state: preferences, project and thread associations, migration records, enrollment metadata, and cached product data.

Behavior

Read into an in-memory Map and persisted through the desktop state-store writer. Field ownership varies; the following sections explain the write path and the dictionary names the observed records.

Evidence
observed + bundle [snapshot]; [bundle-filename]; [bundle-storage]
Limits

The observed file is neither a complete session export nor a public schema. No state mutations or portability tests were performed.

02Which JSON file this explorer describes

The desktop file inspected here is ~/.codex/.codex-global-state.json. No literal codex.json was found in the inspected Codex home. “Codex JSON” is the short name of this explorer, not a new configuration filename. The installed app constructs this filename separately from config.toml.

Official user configuration belongs in ~/.codex/config.toml, with project configuration in .codex/config.toml where supported. This JSON contains desktop preferences, project and thread associations, migration markers, enrollment metadata, and caches. It is neither the transcript of a session nor the complete configuration of the agent.

This is a structural teardown of one observed file and one installed desktop build. Fields absent from the snapshot are not invented to complete a possible schema. Fields present in the snapshot remain listed even when their reader or writer could not be established from the inspected bundle.

observed [docs-config]; [bundle-filename]; [snapshot]

03Objects become folders; leaves become sections

Every object shape has its own folder and standalone index.html. Its page links to its child objects and gives each direct non-object field a named section. A scalar array remains one leaf section; an array containing objects has a child page for the union of its observed item shapes. Empty objects still receive a page. An empty array does not prove a future item schema.

Maps indexed by thread IDs, project IDs, host IDs, account IDs, paths, or arbitrary user-created names use typed placeholders. Repeated members are merged by structural path, including fields seen in only one member. The explorer therefore covers observed structure without generating hundreds of pages named after private identifiers.

Paths use a JSON Pointer-style notation, not filesystem paths. The explorer displays the root as /; a literal JSON Pointer to the document root is the empty string. Slash and tilde inside literal JSON keys use the JSON Pointer escapes ~1 and ~0. Angle-bracket segments represent a family of runtime keys. Folder names are navigation slugs; the visible key and pointer preserve the JSON spelling.

Each leaf records its observed type, meaning, update behavior, and evidence boundary. Source-traced behavior is distinguished from a name-based interpretation. Observing a stored boolean proves its type and presence, but does not prove that changing it enables a feature. Values are omitted: this publication is a dictionary, not an export of the user’s state.

04How the desktop reads and writes this file

The storage class holds an in-memory Map. On startup it reads the primary file, parses JSON, and validates recognized top-level entries against a schema. Invalid recognized entries are dropped with a warning. Unknown keys are retained. A getter can resolve a missing or null stored value through the app’s defaults registry; a raw stored-value getter does not perform that fallback.

If an existing primary file cannot be parsed, the loader tries the .bak file and otherwise starts with an empty Map. When the primary file does not exist, this loader returns an empty Map immediately; that branch does not attempt the backup. A missing key, an explicit false, a null, and an empty object should not be treated as interchangeable.

Set, update, and delete operations modify state and notify listeners. Persistence serializes the Map as a whole JSON object, omitting undefined entries. The persisted-atom container has a 500 ms debounce in this build. Two other state families use microtask coalescing; ordinary keys queue persistence without that debounce. These are internal scheduling choices, not an external write API.

The writer creates a temporary file beside the destination and renames it into place. It then writes the .bak separately. The asynchronous writer’s Windows rename branch retries EPERM, EACCES, or EBUSY after 100, 200, and 400 ms. The source does not establish an interprocess lock, an fsync durability guarantee, or one transaction covering both files.

The update-and-persist path serializes its work through a promise chain, commits the primary file before replacing its in-memory state, and treats a backup failure separately. Flush cancels the atom debounce and waits for the queued persistence work. These details explain why directly editing JSON while the desktop is open can be overwritten by the process’s older in-memory state.

bundle [bundle-storage]

05Commands for inspecting the root shape

The following standard-library Python command prints root key names and their stored JSON types. It does not print values or descend into identifier-keyed maps. It reads the default ~/.codex location unless CODEX_HOME is set. Reading succeeds only where the current user can access the file.

This is an inspection recipe, not a Codex management command. It takes a snapshot of disk; it does not subscribe to in-memory updates. For editing this publication, change the sanitized _content.json beside the explorer and run the renderer from the writings repository root. The renderer never opens the private state file.

python3 - <<'PYCODE'
import json, os
from pathlib import Path
codex_dir = Path(os.environ.get("CODEX_HOME", "~/.codex")).expanduser()
state = json.loads((codex_dir / ".codex-global-state.json").read_text())
def json_type(value):
    if value is None: return "null"
    if isinstance(value, bool): return "boolean"
    if isinstance(value, dict): return "object"
    if isinstance(value, list): return "array"
    if isinstance(value, str): return "string"
    return "number"
print(json.dumps({key: json_type(value) for key, value in state.items()}, indent=2))
PYCODE

# Rebuild this writing from its sanitized editorial source:

06What changing a key actually changes

Use a field’s owning control when one exists. A setting declared by the app registry may have a schema, default, description, access level, and a storage kind: configuration, global-state, or persisted-atom. The storage destination alone does not tell you whether a field is a supported preference, a derived cache, or internal bookkeeping.

Project membership, worktree paths, host enrollment, and migration markers coordinate several stores and services. Editing one JSON field does not demonstrate that the corresponding operation completed elsewhere. Likewise, changing window bounds only changes presentation; changing a cached feature gate does not establish server authorization.

For an investigation requiring an offline edit, first identify the owning writer, expected type, defaults, version, and related records, then close the writer and verify the result through the app. This writing did not perform such edits or test recovery. No CLI named “codex json set” or supported JSON mutation API is claimed here.

For automation, prefer supported settings and session commands. Treat the JSON as diagnostic evidence unless a versioned adapter explicitly owns a narrow read-only projection. Do not use it as a queue, a live event bus, a session transport, or the authority for an external product’s work state.

reconstruction [bundle-storage]; [bundle-registry]; [docs-config]

07Where projects, threads, and hosts meet

Several root families describe different joins. local-projects and remote-projects describe desktop project records. project-order and active-workspace-roots support presentation and selection. thread-project-assignments associates threads with projects. thread-workspace-root-hints, thread-writable-roots, and thread-projectless-output-directories describe path-related context with different purposes.

A selected project is a UI choice. A project ID is an identity. A root path locates files on a particular host. A thread ID identifies a conversation. None of these should be substituted for another. A project may have multiple roots, and a thread can exist outside a saved project.

The app-server project-ID mapping and per-host migration state are evidence of an evolving identity boundary between the desktop and its runtime. Their presence is a reason to preserve host and version provenance. It is not proof that one mapping can be copied to another installation to move a project or resume a session.

Read the record pages for precise observed fields. Empty maps are retained in the explorer because an empty snapshot provides no evidence for their future child schema. The session essay covers the separate runtime database, rollout history, commands, and supported control surfaces.

reconstruction [snapshot]; [bundle-root-keys]

08What this contributes to a session operating system

A useful adapter can extract a small projection: host identity, project reference, thread reference, selected workspace roots, and links to artifacts. Preserve the source version, observation time, and original identifiers privately. Keep this projection separate from the product’s durable work item and from the raw desktop file.

Space or another product should own its work queue, acceptance criteria, scheduling policy, retry state, and result references. The Codex adapter should submit and observe work through an execution interface, while the desktop remains the owner of its preferences and runtime state. A JSON snapshot can assist discovery but cannot certify that a background task is still running.

To offload a task, transfer an explicit request, relevant context, authorization, a workspace or project reference, and an idempotency key. Observe execution and publish a durable result. Do not transfer the full desktop JSON as a task envelope: it mixes unrelated state and may contain drafts, prompts, paths, account metadata, and tokens.

This is a design implication, not an implemented connector. The explorer establishes what state is visible and where meanings are version-dependent. It does not implement migration, scheduling, cross-product authentication, unattended execution, or recovery.

proposal [snapshot]; [bundle-storage]

35Sources and limits

Observed structure comes from one read-only local snapshot on 3 October 2026. Behavioral explanations cite the installed ChatGPT desktop bundle, version26.928.31416 (12553), or are explicitly marked as inference. Official documentation is used only for supported configuration boundaries. The folder representation and operating-system implications are reconstructions or proposals.

All primitive values and identifying dynamic keys were omitted. Repeated objects and object-array items are unions of every observed member, including empty structures; embedded tool-schema property maps use placeholders. The original file was not edited. Features absent from the snapshot, server behavior, offline editing, and restoration were not tested. The published content is versioned research, not a supported global-state API.

  1. [snapshot] Observed local state structure

    $CODEX_HOME/.codex-global-state.json

    Read-only snapshot on 3 October 2026. Static keys, types, and counts were retained; primitive values and identifying map keys were withheld. All entries were traversed, with unions of repeated shapes.

    Locator: pCe / mCe / D7; inspected character offset 2145996
